entries.rationale: <module>: MPLCONFIGDIR defaults via os.environ.setdefault to the literal /tmp/hexafe-plotstats-matplotlib, before importing Matplotlib. This opt-in developer benchmark generates synthetic datasets; an existing environment override wins. The path is shared/predictable, not process-scoped or automatically cleaned. Renewal accepts local benchmark cache integrity risk on a trusted single-user runner; it is unsuitable for hostile shared /tmp execution.

<module>: MPLCONFIGDIR is the literal /tmp/hexafe-plotstats-matplotlib set only when the environment has no override, before Matplotlib import. _build_cases uses seeded synthetic arrays and PNG benchmarks, not customer inputs. This remains a predictable shared cache directory with no process cleanup guarantee; renewal is limited to trusted single-user benchmark execution, retaining shared-/tmp integrity risk.

main: The --output default is the literal /tmp/hexafe_plotstats_renderer_comparisons; the explicit CLI option controls output_dir. main creates it with mkdir(exist_ok=True) and writes only synthetic comparison PNG/JSON/Markdown artifacts from _cases. There is no process uniqueness/cleanup or no-clobber guarantee; renewal accepts predictable-output integrity/overwrite risk only for opt-in trusted single-user runs, not hostile shared /tmp.

<module>: MPLCONFIGDIR is the fixed /tmp/hexafe-plotstats-matplotlib default applied by setdefault before Matplotlib import; an operator may override it. _cases generates synthetic renderer comparisons. The cache path is predictable/shared and has no process cleanup contract; accepted only for opt-in trusted single-user developer/CI benchmarks, with shared-/tmp integrity risk retained.

benchmark_csv_summary_large_data_probe: scope_query comes from TabularSqliteStore.source_row_number_query_for_group_search on the synthetic CSV benchmark store; the builder quotes columns and binds filter/search values, and scope_params is passed unchanged to execute.

benchmark_sqlite_grouping_high_cardinality_probe: scope_query comes from store.source_row_number_query_for_group_search for the synthetic high-cardinality benchmark; TabularSqliteStore quotes identifiers and emits bound search/filter values, supplied separately as scope_params.

fetch_model: url is supplied only by main from the three HTTPS URL constants in RAPIDOCR_MODEL_ASSET_MANIFEST in header_ocr_backend; the CLI exposes output-dir and force, not URLs. expected_sha256 comes from the same manifest and is verified before replacing the destination. This is a trusted developer downloader API, not a URL ingestion endpoint; urllib redirects remain enabled.

_prepare_export_snapshot: snapshot_table_name consists only of the fixed _export_snapshot_ prefix, integer milliseconds and id(self). self.filter_query is the application-generated measurement scope from ExportDialog/FilterDialog via build_measurement_filter_query/build_measurement_export_query (or the analytical partition wrapper); filter literals are escaped by _escape_sql_literal and expression identifiers/operators are validated by the filter compiler. No raw SQL editor/file field feeds this path; arbitrary SQL callers are outside this internal API contract.

_prepare_export_snapshot: snapshot_table_name is generated in _prepare_export_snapshot exclusively from the fixed _export_snapshot_ prefix, integer milliseconds and id(self); it contains no user/file/database text.

_build_scoped_export_query: filter_query is an internal SQL scope supplied by ExportDataThread from report_query_service builders or its generated snapshot SELECT. FilterDialog compiles the filter DSL and escapes literal values; this wrapper is SQL composition, not sanitization and must not accept raw external SQL.

build_analytical_partition_query: missing_reference is the local constant NULLIF(TRIM(REFERENCE), empty string) IS NULL. filter_query comes from ExportDataThread application scope builders, which compile filter expressions and escape literals; report IDs/references are read as data by the CASE expressions, never interpolated here.

fetch_partition_values: quoted_partition is quote_identifier(partition_column), which doubles embedded double quotes; scoped_query comes from _build_scoped_export_query over the application-generated export/snapshot scope. Raw external SQL is not an accepted scope source.

fetch_partition_header_counts: quoted_partition uses db.quote_identifier(partition_column); validated_header_expr is accepted only by _validated_partition_header_expression against the one-element _PARTITION_HEADER_EXPRESSIONS allowlist. scoped_query wraps the generated export/snapshot SELECT through _build_scoped_export_query, not external SQL.

load_export_partition_dataframe: scoped_query wraps the internal generated export/snapshot SELECT via _build_scoped_export_query; quoted_partition is db.quote_identifier(partition_column). partition_value is separately bound as a single ? parameter.

fetch_sql_measurement_summary: scoped_query is produced by _build_scoped_export_query over the application-generated export/snapshot SELECT. usl, lsl, reference, header and ax remain five bound parameters; no measurement/reference value is interpolated into this summary.

fetch_sql_measurement_summaries: scoped_query is the internal export/snapshot scope from _build_scoped_export_query. where_clause is chosen locally between the empty string and WHERE REFERENCE = ?; an optional reference is passed in params, never in SQL text.

list_events._list: where joins only local detector_key = ?, signal_id = ? and status = ? fragments; _validate_status checks status and values are in params. limit_clause is empty or the literal LIMIT ? with _positive_limit supplied separately.

recent_events_by_signal._list: where is a local list beginning with signal_id = ? and optionally status = ? after _validate_status. Signal ID, status and _positive_limit(limit) are all passed in params; joining the list adds no caller SQL.

list_artifacts._list: where joins only locally generated artifact_key/model_type/signal_id/status = ? predicates. status is validated, all filter values are bound, and limit_clause is empty or LIMIT ? with a positive bound limit.

_load_dynamic_values_for_records: record_placeholders and field_placeholders are comma-joined literal ? markers sized from bounded record/field chunks. Actual record IDs and field names are in tuple(record_chunk) + tuple(field_chunk); require_identifier also validates field_names.

_load_fixed_production_frame: select_columns is built from PRODUCTION_RECORD_COLUMNS plus schema-present extra_columns after require_identifier; every source column and alias passes db.quote_identifier. where_sql uses _fixed_filter_sql fixed columns and bound values via _append_in_filter.

_load_dynamic_metric_discovery_rows: where_sql is built from _fixed_filter_sql: fixed records column names and _append_in_filter question-mark lists, with all ProductionFilterState values in params. No dynamic field/value is embedded in SQL.

_load_fixed_metric_discovery_rows: field_name passes require_identifier and db.quote_identifier (imported as _quote_identifier). where_sql comes from _fixed_filter_sql using fixed records columns and bound IN values via _append_in_filter; metric values remain data.

list_source_profiles._list_profiles: where_clause is chosen locally between empty and WHERE is_enabled = 1 from the include_disabled boolean; none of the profile configuration or database strings enter the SQL text.
latest_sync_run._latest: profile_filter is empty or the fixed WHERE runs.source_profile_id = ?; source_profile_id is passed separately in params, not interpolated.

upsert_industrial_records_from_rows._upsert_rows: placeholders consists only of ? markers for the bounded key_chunk. source_profile_id, source_db_alias and every source_record_key are separately bound in (source_profile_id, source_db_alias, *key_chunk).

upsert_industrial_records_from_rows._upsert_rows: placeholders is generated solely from literal ? for key_chunk length. Profile ID, source alias and source record keys are bound separately; database-origin keys do not become query text.

upsert_industrial_records_from_rows._upsert_rows: placeholders is a comma-separated sequence of ? sized from record_id_chunk. All record IDs are bound via tuple(record_id_chunk); no identifier or data interpolation occurs.
summarize_counts._counts: profile_filter is empty or the literal WHERE source_profile_id = ? selected in _counts; the profile ID is supplied in params. The sync-runs table is a fixed schema name.
summarize_counts._counts: profile_filter is the same empty/fixed WHERE source_profile_id = ? branch in _counts; the profile ID is bound in params. The industrial_records table is fixed in source.

load_cached_industrial_dataframe: select_columns is assembled exclusively from _CACHE_RECORD_ID_COLUMN, INDUSTRIAL_EXPORT_COLUMNS and the fixed ir.raw_record_json expression; all identifiers are module constants, not cached data or requested dynamic fields.

_prepare_cached_export_scope: _EXPORT_SCOPE_TABLE and _EXPORT_REFERENCE_FILTER_TABLE are module constants. reference_column has passed _resolve_filter_column and membership in INDUSTRIAL_FILTER_RECORD_COLUMNS. filter_sql comes from _cached_query_filter_where_clause with table_alias=ir, validated operator enums and bound values in filter_params.

_append_cached_dynamic_columns: placeholders is generated from literal ? for a bounded chunk of cached record IDs; chunk is supplied separately to execute, so cached values cannot change SQL structure.

_cached_query_filter_clause: table_alias is supplied only as the literal ir by every internal export caller (six call sites in this module). Dynamic column is a bound rv_filter.field_name parameter; operators are validated by IndustrialQueryFilter.validated and values remain bound in the enclosing predicate.
_cached_export_dynamic_fields: _EXPORT_SCOPE_TABLE is a module constant. rv.field_name values are returned as data; no database field name is interpolated into this SELECT.
_prepare_cached_export_scope: _EXPORT_SCOPE_TABLE is the fixed module-owned temporary scope table name; no user or cached record data contributes to the interpolated identifier.

_attach_cached_dynamic_values: id_placeholders and field_placeholders are generated solely from ? markers sized from record_ids/dynamic_fields. All cached IDs and field names are bound in (*record_ids, *dynamic_fields).

_prepare_cached_export_scope: _EXPORT_SCOPE_TABLE/_EXPORT_REFERENCE_FILTER_TABLE are module-owned temp names. _append_filter_sql only changes the prefix of the generated _cached_query_filter_where_clause result (fixed ir alias, allowlisted fixed columns or bound dynamic field names, validated operators); reference_column and all filter values are bound in params.

_prepare_cached_export_scope: _EXPORT_SCOPE_TABLE is a module constant; filter_sql is generated by _cached_query_filter_where_clause with fixed ir alias, fixed-column allowlist or bound dynamic field lookup and validated operator enums. filter_params carries every value.

_iter_cached_export_batches: select_columns is built only from fixed ir.id, INDUSTRIAL_EXPORT_COLUMNS and ir.raw_record_json. _EXPORT_SCOPE_TABLE is a module constant; requested dynamic fields are attached separately via bound queries.

load_cached_industrial_dataframe: base_query uses only module-owned INDUSTRIAL_EXPORT_COLUMNS and _CACHE_RECORD_ID_COLUMN. _append_filter_sql(filter_sql) transforms the WHERE built by _cached_query_filter_where_clause: fixed allowlisted columns, validated IndustrialQueryFilter operators and bound values. Dynamic reference_column is bound as rv.field_name = ?; table_alias is the literal ir.

materialize_industrial_report_links: report_expr and industrial_expr are looked up in fixed REPORT_FIELD_SQL/INDUSTRIAL_FIELD_SQL maps after validate_join_rule. time_clause comes from _time_window_clause using fixed timestamp expressions or empty text; time_window_seconds, rule IDs/names/field labels and timestamps are bound parameters.

_load_or_refresh_tabular_metadata: _INDUSTRIAL_TABULAR_METADATA_TABLE is a module constant passed through this module's _quote_identifier (double-quote escaping). scope_key is bound as ?, and metadata JSON remains data.

_dynamic_field_view_expression: Database-origin field_name is encoded by _sql_literal (single quotes doubled); output_column is escaped with _quote_identifier. The correlated SELECT shape is fixed. No database string is treated as raw expression SQL.

_refresh_value_facets: where_sql is generated by load_industrial_cache_tabular_result from fixed records.source_profile_id/source_db_alias IN predicates and ? lists; scope params are passed unchanged to execute.

_load_or_refresh_tabular_metadata: _INDUSTRIAL_TABULAR_METADATA_TABLE is a module constant escaped by _quote_identifier. scope key, counters and dynamic-field JSON are all bound parameters; database-derived field names are not SQL fragments here.
_refresh_value_facets: _INDUSTRIAL_TABULAR_VALUE_FACETS_TABLE is a fixed module identifier quoted by _quote_identifier; scope_key is bound as ?. This DELETE does not interpolate a cache key.

_dynamic_field_names: prefix is empty or source_db., supplied only as the fixed source_db ATTACH alias by _write_tabular_sqlite_from_industrial_cache. where_sql is the fixed-column source-profile/source-alias scope from load_industrial_cache_tabular_result, with values bound in params.
_ensure_value_facets_for_scope: _INDUSTRIAL_TABULAR_VALUE_FACETS_TABLE is a module constant quoted by _quote_identifier. scope_key is bound; no cached column names or values enter the SELECT text.

_dynamic_field_metadata: value_expr and _NUMERIC_VALUE_SQL are local constants (TRIM/COALESCE and the numeric-text CASE over field_value). where_sql is the generated fixed source-profile/source-alias scope with ? lists, and all profile IDs/aliases are supplied separately in params.

_insert_base_value_facets: _INDUSTRIAL_TABULAR_VALUE_FACETS_TABLE is a module constant quoted by _quote_identifier. normalized_expr comes from _normalized_value_sql(expression) where expression is a fixed _BASE_INDUSTRIAL_COLUMNS SQL expression. scope_key and output column label are bound as data.

_write_tabular_sqlite_from_industrial_cache: where_sql comes from load_industrial_cache_tabular_result: fixed source_profile_id/source_db_alias predicates with ? lists. IDs and aliases are separately bound as params; source_db is a fixed ATTACH alias.

_insert_industrial_tabular_rows: selected_columns is fixed _BASE_INDUSTRIAL_COLUMNS expressions plus _quote_identifier aliases. where_sql uses fixed profile/alias predicates and bound params; _INDUSTRIAL_TABULAR_TABLE is constant and quoted. output_columns and selected_output_columns quote every database-derived output name using _quote_identifier, and dynamic field selectors are bound in (*params, *dynamic_fields).

_metadata_scope_fingerprint: where_sql is the generated fixed records source-profile/source-alias IN scope from load_industrial_cache_tabular_result; the joined value-table contents never enter SQL text, and scope values are bound in params.

_insert_dynamic_value_facets: _INDUSTRIAL_TABULAR_VALUE_FACETS_TABLE is module-owned and quoted by _quote_identifier. normalized_expr wraps the local constant COALESCE(NULLIF(values_row.field_value_text, empty string), values_row.field_value_json) through _normalized_value_sql. Output columns come from a TEMP mapping table filled with bound parameters (field name, output column), never from SQL text; scope_key is bound as ?.

_metadata_scope_fingerprint: where_sql originates in load_industrial_cache_tabular_result with only fixed source_profile_id/source_db_alias IN predicates and ? marker lists; all profile IDs/aliases are passed in params.

_create_industrial_tabular_view: view_name uses the module prefix plus uuid4().hex and is escaped by _quote_identifier. selected_columns uses fixed _BASE_INDUSTRIAL_COLUMNS expressions, quoted output aliases and _dynamic_field_view_expression (field names via _sql_literal). view_where_sql comes from _literal_where_sql on fixed profile/alias predicates; reviewed fix splits templates before escaping values so embedded ? never re-enters substitution. SQL literals use doubled single quotes, with IDs normalized to int.

build_bounded_poll_query: columns_sql quotes _validated_selected_columns via _quote_identifier; table_name uses _quote_dotted_identifier(profile.source_object_name). cursor/tie_breaker also use _quote_identifier; those helpers call require_identifier/require_dotted_identifier before dialect quoting. where is generated only from fixed resume predicates and those validated identifiers. Offset values and cycle limit are bound; dialect selects fixed TOP/LIMIT query shapes.

build_bounded_poll_query: columns_sql quotes _validated_selected_columns via _quote_identifier; table_name uses _quote_dotted_identifier(profile.source_object_name). cursor/tie_breaker also use _quote_identifier; those helpers call require_identifier/require_dotted_identifier before dialect quoting. where is generated only from fixed resume predicates and those validated identifiers. Offset values and cycle limit are bound; dialect selects fixed TOP/LIMIT query shapes.

read_events_after._read: event_type_clause is empty or fixed AND event_type IN with comma-joined ? markers. Event types, source profile, stream key, after-event ID and safe limit are supplied in params; event payloads never enter SQL text.

list_dead_letters._list: where_clause joins only = ? predicates for the local consumer_key/source_profile_id/stream_key/status column tuple; caller values are passed in params, and no column name comes from the caller.

list_configs._list: where_clause joins only local enabled = 1 and source_profile_id = ? strings. The optional profile ID is normalized to int and separately bound; config JSON and stream names are not interpolated.

anomaly_counts_by_severity._count: where_clause is constructed by _append_event_filters from fixed events.status/signal_id/detector_key/severity = ? strings; status and severity are allowlisted, signal ID normalized and every requested value bound in params.

anomaly_counts_by_detector._count: where_clause is constructed by _append_event_filters from fixed events.status/signal_id/detector_key/severity = ? strings; status and severity are allowlisted, signal ID normalized and every requested value bound in params.

signal_timeline_window._list: where joins fixed samples.signal_id = ? with optional fixed samples.event_time >= ? and <= ? strings; signal ID, canonical UTC boundaries and _positive_limit(limit) are bound. Timeline sample values are not SQL fragments.

_aggregate_rows_from_cursor: where_clause is empty or fixed WHERE samples.signal_id IN with ? markers sized from signal_ids. limit_clause is empty or fixed LIMIT ? with _positive_limit; IDs and limit are separately bound in params.

_snapshot_timelines: selected_values is generated solely from comma-joined (?) marker groups sized from signal_ids. Actual IDs and the timeline limit are bound in (*signal_ids, limit); no event/sample values are embedded.

_snapshot_recent_events: selected_values is a sequence of literal (?) marker groups, with IDs/limit bound as (*signal_ids, limit). _DASHBOARD_EVENT_SELECT is the fixed module SELECT/JOIN constant, not event data or caller SQL.

list_samples_by_ids._list: placeholders is a literal ? sequence sized from a bounded chunk of int-normalized sample IDs. Actual IDs are supplied as chunk; raw record data never enters the SELECT text.

list_signal_definitions_by_ids._list: placeholders contains only ? markers sized from a bounded chunk of int-normalized signal IDs; execute receives chunk separately. Signal configuration strings do not enter SQL text.
list_recent_samples._list: where is fixed WHERE signal_id = ? plus optional AND segment_key_json = ?; normalized signal ID, JSON-serialized segment_key and safe_limit are all bound in params.

list_samples_before._list: where uses the fixed signal_id and (event_time,id) boundary predicate, plus optional segment_key_json = ?. Signal ID, canonical boundary time, sample ID, JSON segment key and safe limit are bound separately.

_latest_sample._get: placeholders is comma-joined literal ? sized from config.signal_keys. config.source_profile_id and each signal key are bound in (config.source_profile_id, *config.signal_keys); no config string becomes SQL text.

resolve_characteristic_aliases_bulk: alias_name_placeholders is a ? list; scope_where is either fixed scope_type = global or a fixed global/reference predicate with a ? list from reference count. Actual alias names and references are supplied as tuple(params), not interpolated.

fetch_distinct_references: source_sql is a fixed SELECT chosen by _measurement_source_sql after view/table existence checks. _REFERENCE_SQL is a module expression constant; reference strings are evaluated as data and never interpolated.

_metric_source_cte: source_sql is selected by _measurement_source_sql from three fixed view/current-table/legacy-table SELECT shapes after schema probes. _METRIC_IDENTITY_SQL and _REFERENCE_SQL are module constants; measurement/reference data is evaluated by SQL, not inserted as SQL text. STEP3 T15 adds only a runtime-selected literal MATERIALIZED keyword (or empty string) from the SQLite version check; no data-derived syntax is introduced. Owner and expiry are unchanged.

fetch_mapping_impact_counts: _metric_source_cte(source_sql) uses the fixed schema-dependent _measurement_source_sql result plus module identity/reference constants. where_clause is fixed metric_name = ? plus optional AND reference = ? after normalize_alias_scope; alias and scope value are bound.

fetch_distinct_report_metric_names: _metric_source_cte(source_sql) composes a source chosen by _measurement_source_sql from fixed view/current/legacy SELECT shapes plus _METRIC_IDENTITY_SQL/_REFERENCE_SQL constants. The sample-reference limit is bound as a parameter; metric and reference contents remain database values.

count_query_scope_rows: scope.sql is the internal QueryScope SQL produced by TabularSqliteStore.query_scope: table/column names are quoted, predicate operators compiled from the filter model and values bound in scope.params. row_count_sql is likewise generated by that builder. QueryScope is a trusted SQL composition contract, not an external raw-query ingestion API.

build_value_update_statements: quoted_table and quoted_column come from db.quote_identifier, doubling embedded double quotes. Normalization callers choose names from NORMALIZATION_TARGETS, and old/new values are bound as ?. Even direct identifier arguments cannot break quoting.

_build_legacy_update_statements: quoted_table and quoted_key use db.quote_identifier. assignments is built only from field_columns lookups in LEGACY_REPORT_FIELD_COLUMNS/LEGACY_MEASUREMENT_FIELD_COLUMNS with every column quoted and an appended = ?. record_id and field values remain bound.

build_grouping_scope_query_from_filter_state: select_clause and _GROUPING_REPORT_VIEW are source constants. where_clauses here are only reference/part_name predicates from _build_in_clause, which inserts values solely inside single-quoted literals escaped by _escape_sql_literal. The richer filter branch delegates to the validated measurement filter builder.

build_distinct_value_query: quoted_column uses db.quote_identifier(column_name), including embedded-double-quote escaping. source is a generated filtered scope from build_measurement_export_query/_distinct_filter_scope, a fixed optimized join, or db.quote_identifier(source_view). Filter scopes come from application builders with validated DSL/escaped literals; no caller identifier can break out of quoting after the reviewed fix.

build_measurement_export_query: _MEASUREMENT_EXPORT_SELECT_FROM_VIEW and _MEASUREMENT_EXPORT_VIEW are module constants. normalized_filter_query is the compiled application report scope from FilterDialog/FilterState, with allowlisted DSL identifiers/operators and _escape_sql_literal values, not external raw SQL.

build_measurement_export_query: _MEASUREMENT_EXPORT_SELECT_FROM_SCOPE is a fixed module column list. normalized_filter_query is the application-generated measurement SELECT scope; filter values use _escape_sql_literal and expressions use the validated filter compiler. Raw external SQL is outside this helper contract.

build_measurement_filter_query: _MEASUREMENT_EXPORT_SELECT_FROM_VIEW and _MEASUREMENT_EXPORT_VIEW are fixed module constants. Subsequent filters use only local column names, _escape_sql_literal for values/dates and parse_filter_expression with _MEASUREMENT_FILTER_COLUMNS followed by the safe SQL compiler for user expressions.

_append_industrial_context_to_export_query: normalized_base_query is built internally by build_measurement_export_query via build_industrial_measurement_export_query. It uses fixed view/column constants and validated filter DSL with escaped data literals; industrial identifiers in this wrapper are fixed schema names. No industrial metadata becomes SQL text.

_build_select_from_view: select_clause is selected only by the internal report/grouping/measurement builders from fixed source SELECT lists; view_name is one of the module-owned _REPORT_OVERVIEW_VIEW/_GROUPING_REPORT_VIEW/_MEASUREMENT_EXPORT_VIEW constants. No filter text enters this base SELECT.

build_grouping_query: normalized_filter_query is the application-generated FilterDialog/FilterState SELECT scope with validated DSL identifiers/operators and literals escaped by _escape_sql_literal. The caller path supplies compiled scope SQL, not a raw query field; _normalize_sql_query itself is not a sanitizer.

_build_select_from_view: select_clause is an internal fixed column-list argument. normalized_filter_query comes from the generated FilterDialog scope (build_measurement_filter_query/build_grouping_scope_query_from_filter_state); DSL identifiers/operators are validated and data literals use _escape_sql_literal. _normalize_sql_query only trims terminators; arbitrary external SQL is outside this composition API.

_ensure_canonical_timestamp_storage: quoted_table/quoted_column come from _quote_identifier over fixed _CANONICAL_TIMESTAMP_COLUMNS table/column names, additionally checked against sqlite_master/PRAGMA table_info. Stored timestamp text is fetched as data, never used as an identifier.

_ensure_canonical_timestamp_storage: quoted_table/quoted_column are escaped by _quote_identifier from the fixed _CANONICAL_TIMESTAMP_COLUMNS map, with schema existence checks. Canonical timestamps and row IDs are bound in updates via executemany.

_ensure_sync_run_status_constraint: column_list is generated by _quote_identifier over the local fixed tuple of industrial_sync_runs migration columns. Both table names and the SELECT/INSERT shape are fixed; no schema-derived or record-derived names are inserted.

build_grouping_query: normalized_filter_query is the application FilterDialog/FilterState generated scope with validated filter expressions and escaped literals; this compatibility fallback is used only if the canonical report_query_service grouping helper is unavailable. Trimming in _normalize_filter_query is not sanitization and external raw SQL is not a valid caller input.

build_grouping_query: _GROUPING_SCOPE_SELECT is the module-owned fixed grouping report column list. vw_grouping_reports is a fixed schema view; the fallback unfiltered SELECT contains no external fragment.

assignments.read: table_name is passed to this local read closure by _prepare_effective_table after _quote_identifier(self.table_name); the default identifier uses a UUID hex token and caller overrides are still escaped. Group-name filters and preview limits, where present, are bound parameters, not SQL text.

group_counts.read: table_name is passed to this local read closure by _prepare_effective_table after _quote_identifier(self.table_name); the default identifier uses a UUID hex token and caller overrides are still escaped. Group-name filters and preview limits, where present, are bound parameters, not SQL text.

group_counts.read: table_name is passed to this local read closure by _prepare_effective_table after _quote_identifier(self.table_name); the default identifier uses a UUID hex token and caller overrides are still escaped. Group-name filters and preview limits, where present, are bound parameters, not SQL text.

group_members.read: table_name is passed to this local read closure by _prepare_effective_table after _quote_identifier(self.table_name); the default identifier uses a UUID hex token and caller overrides are still escaped. Group-name filters and preview limits, where present, are bound parameters, not SQL text.

group_members.read: table_name is passed to this local read closure by _prepare_effective_table after _quote_identifier(self.table_name); the default identifier uses a UUID hex token and caller overrides are still escaped. Group-name filters and preview limits, where present, are bound parameters, not SQL text.

_prepare_effective_table: table_name is _quote_identifier(self.table_name); the default name is a fixed prefix plus uuid.uuid4().hex and overrides have double quotes escaped. This reset DELETE embeds no group or row data.
_apply_command: table_name is already escaped by _prepare_effective_table via _quote_identifier. command.group_name is bound as ? for DeleteGroupingGroup; it cannot alter SQL structure.

_apply_command: table_name is escaped by _prepare_effective_table via _quote_identifier; replacement group name, replacement color and original group name are all separately bound for RenameGroupingGroup.

_apply_rows_command: table_name is escaped by _prepare_effective_table via _quote_identifier. Row ID, group name and color are bound in executemany; ON CONFLICT SQL is fixed in source.

_apply_scope_command: scope_table is _quote_identifier(self._scope_table_name), whose name is a fixed prefix plus the per-store uuid.uuid4().hex token. No command or source-row content contributes to this identifier.

_apply_scope_command: scope_table uses _quote_identifier on the UUID-based _scope_table_name. query comes only from _scope_query: TabularSqliteStore generated quoted-identifier/bound-filter queries or _selected_group_keys_query. _apply_scope_command: table_name comes quoted from _prepare_effective_table and scope_table from _quote_identifier(self._scope_table_name); UUID defaults and overrides cannot escape identifier quotes. command.group_name and command.color are bound parameters.

_apply_scope_command: table_name is quoted by _prepare_effective_table and scope_table by _quote_identifier; names are UUID-based unless explicitly overridden, still quoted. Group name and color are supplied as ? values to the INSERT SELECT.

_selected_group_keys_query: row_column is _quote_identifier(source_row_number). base_scope.sql comes from TabularSqliteStore.query_scope with quoted names and bound filters. predicate is generated by _selected_key_predicate using quoted selector columns and ? lists; selected key values join base_scope.params as key_params.

preview_value_rows: grouped_query is built locally in preview_value_rows from quoted self.table_name, _sqlite_normalized_value_expr of a known column and generated _where_clause/LIKE ? filters. Search/filter values remain bound; optional limits are int-normalized.
